input.title: [harness] check-hooks-registered prints 'env: ahead of the pinned bar' before a runtime check that then fails
input.body:
Since TKT-9101, check-hooks-registered prints "env: ahead of the pinned bar" on stdout before it runs the env's runtime checks (the hook script, the git hook list, the wrapper, the PATH line). When one of those checks then fails, the output reads "ahead" and then FAIL. The exit code is right (non-zero), but the first line reads like a pass to someone scanning it.

Found by the TKT-9101 captain. Fix: print the "ahead" note with the final verdict line, or only when the whole verdict passes. Add a black-box case where the env is ahead but a runtime check fails, and assert the output never shows "ahead" as the verdict.

input.title: judgment-eval cannot measure a question-set version before it deploys
input.body:
judgment-eval runs a use case against the question-set version the server has deployed, and a dev server has no model key. So a proposed version (vN+1) cannot be measured until it merges and deploys.

Measured on TKT-9102: a v2 question set was gated, merged and deployed with its acceptance number recorded as n/a, because nothing could produce it before deploy. The post-deploy eval then failed the bar set in advance (1 of 3 overrides fixed), so the change has to be reverted in prod. A measurement before merge would have stopped it at the PR.

Every future "propose question-set vN+1" ticket hits the same gap.

Fix direction: let judgment-eval score a candidate question set that is not deployed (for example, an eval endpoint that accepts a candidate version id and scores it without recording product calls), so the number exists before merge. Regression test: an eval naming a non-deployed version scores against that version, and a version it cannot load is an error, not a silent fallback to the deployed set.

input.title: credo no_unscoped_log_refute cannot see a generic phrase bound to an attribute or variable
input.body:
The widened credo check from TKT-9103 flags a literal phrase refuted on a whole log capture in an async test module. It does not see a phrase that is first bound to a module attribute or a variable and then refuted.

Measured by the TKT-9103 captain: one test's @body ("Pick up the dry cleaning before noon; the ticket is in the car.") is refuted unscoped, and differs from another async test's body text by one capital letter. It is not a collision today, but one edit away from a cross-test false failure, and the check cannot flag it.

Fix direction: either resolve a module attribute or local binding to its literal before judging, or scope these refutes (own entries only) so the class is closed for bound values too. Regression test: a bound generic phrase refuted on a whole capture in an async module is flagged; a scoped one is not.

input.title: Session-mention parity: U+180E is whitespace in the server router but not in the harness labeller
input.body:
The session-mention grammar differs between the server router and the harness labeller on one character, U+180E (Mongolian vowel separator). Elixir's \s under the u flag matches U+180E; Ruby's \s does not, and U+180E is not in \p{Zs}, so the harness normalizer does not map it either. So "harness:<U+180E>x" routes as harness on the server but labels as no mention in the harness labeller, and the eval would score it.

Reproduced by the TKT-9104 reviewer. It predates the current grammar version. A code comment saying \s means the same ASCII set is false for this character.

Fix: map U+180E to a space in both copies, fix the comment, and add a parity vector to both vector lists.

input.title: athena dev seed prints a minted machine client token to stdout
input.body:
The dev setup script (the athena dev seed) mints a machine client token and prints its value to stdout ("seeds: minted client token for dev-laptop ..." followed by the token). Any captured dev-setup or gate log then holds a working dev credential, and agents capture these logs routinely.

Observed by the TKT-9105 captain, who did not read the value and deleted the log. Scope: a local dev credential, not a prod one.

Fix direction: write the token to a 0600 file and print only the path (and the token's id or fingerprint, never its value). Regression test: the seed's stdout never contains the minted token value.

input.title: Ingress advisory-lock waits (event idempotency, priorities identity) have no lock_timeout and hold a Repo connection
input.body:
Impact: an ingress webhook (Slack events, Slack interactions, forge events) that waits on the event store's idempotency advisory lock, or on the priorities item-identity advisory lock, holds a Repo connection for as long as it waits, with no lock_timeout. The prod pool is 3 (TKT-9106), so a few stuck waiters can starve every other path: the same class as an earlier prod outage (TKT-9107) and TKT-9108. TKT-9108 bounded only the Slack conversation lock (SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '1000ms' -> storage_failed).

Unbounded pg_advisory_xact_lock waits left:
- EventStore.lock_idempotency_key/2, called by the Slack event router, the Slack interactions handler and the forge events adapter (webhook ingress, inside each caller's own transaction).
- Priorities.IndexStore.lock_identity/3, called from three ingest/upsert paths.
- SettingsStore.lock_mode/2 and the eval store's series lock: owner-driven admin and eval writes, rare contention; lower priority.
- Fleet.PolicyStore: owner's fleet policy saves; rare contention.
Other umbrella apps have their own Repos, not this pool.

Fix: bound each ingress-path wait with SET LOCAL lock_timeout inside its transaction (before the lock), map 55P03 lock_not_available to that path's existing retryable failure (a 5xx for a webhook), and prove it with a second-connection holder so the wait is real and no verdict depends on a clock. Consider one shared helper so every advisory lock states its bound.

input.title: [gen_saas] async athena tests refute generic phrases on an unscoped capture_log (connection lost, credit balance, hooks.slack.com)
input.body:
Async athena tests refute generic phrases against the whole capture_log capture. Any concurrent test that logs the same phrase fails them. This is the TKT-9109 / TKT-9110 class, and neither the TKT-9109 sweep nor its credo check reached these sites. Sites (apps/athena/test, as of origin/main 0000abcd):
- slack/post_claim_manager_test.exs refutes "connection lost"; five async files log it.
- slack_events/topic_routing_integration_test.exs refutes "secret words"; another async test logs "work secret words".
- priorities/summaries/port/anthropic_test.exs refutes "credit balance"; priorities/summaries_test.exs refutes "credit balance is too low" and "echo of".
- slack_interactions_test.exs and slack_interactions/click_worker_test.exs refute "hooks.slack.com".

Found by the TKT-9110 captain. No instance has failed in CI yet. These are flake risks read from the code.

Fix: scope each refute to the test's own entries, and prove each fix with a deterministic foreign-line injection that fails first. Then widen the credo check so a literal-phrase refute on an unscoped capture in an async module is flagged. No retry, skip, async: false mask or loosened assertion.

input.title: Flaky: suite-reaper S13/S14 fail under load, turned custom main RED at 0000beef
input.body:
custom origin/main went RED at 0000beef (main-health): harness-gate failed 1 of 165 checks, scripts/test/suite-reaper/self-test.sh, 103.3s wall, load1 about 24-27.

Failure lines from the main-health log:
- FAIL S13 an orphaned exec-spinner never survives suite_reap_tagged
- FAIL S14 a scan that cannot run fails the reap loudly: rc=1 survivors=1234:sleep 309, err=suite-reaper: cannot read the process scanner /nonexistent/proc-env-scan.awk.
- VERDICT: FAIL (2 failed, 26 passed)

Not caused by the landing: 0000beef (TKT-9111) changes only two Ruby libs, two help texts, a contract and one self-test; nothing under scripts/. The previous tip was GREEN minutes earlier. One functional re-run of the same self-test on 0000beef in a clean lane at load1 about 10 passed (28 cases). That re-run is evidence the verdict depends on machine load, not a fix.

Suspect: S13's orphaned exec-spinner and the reap's /proc scan race under load (a process mid-exec reads empty environ), so a tagged process survives the reap; S14's survivor may be S13's leftover leaking into the next case.

Fix: make S13 and S14 verdicts deterministic (block on the event, inject the scan state, or isolate each case's processes), never a retry, a longer timeout as the verdict, or a skip. If the reap itself can miss a mid-exec process in production, fix the reap too. Regression evidence must show the old test failing on a deterministic reproduction of the race, not under load.
